variants.title: Run the evidence loop
variants.context: The evidence loop runs from a scientific specification, through an evidence factory that versions data and solves, into a structured model, then a validation laboratory that challenges the claim, and only then bounded use with a trusted fallback.
variants.prompt: A team wants a surrogate for an expensive reactor simulation. Put the loop in order.

items.text: Release inside an explicit envelope, detect extrapolation, and route unsupported cases to the trusted solver.
Choose a representation and objective suited to the operator, inverse problem, or hybrid correction.
Test held out regimes, constraint residuals, uncertainty calibration, and matched accuracy baselines.
Version the experiments, simulation settings, meshes, solver tolerances, and provenance for every sample.
State the variables, units, geometry, governing relations, tolerances, and the decision the output serves.

variants.hint: Which step decides what counts as credible evidence in the first place?
variants.explanation: The specification defines tolerance and regime, so validation has something concrete to fail against before any release.

variants.title: Run the evidence loop
variants.context: The evidence loop runs from a scientific specification, through an evidence factory that versions data and solves, into a structured model, then a validation laboratory that challenges the claim, and only then bounded use with a trusted fallback.
variants.prompt: Validation finds that the surrogate violates a boundary condition in one corner of the envelope. Put the response in order.

items.text: Retrain with the boundary term represented in the structure or objective rather than left implicit.
Recheck the corner, the neighboring regimes, and the constraint residuals on protected cases.
Release with the corner inside the envelope only if the evidence supports it, and route the rest to the solver.
Generate additional versioned solves that sample the corner and the transition into it.
Reread the specification to confirm which boundary condition and tolerance actually apply in that corner.

variants.hint: Validation can send a candidate back to data design or model design, not only to training.
variants.explanation: A failed constraint reopens the evidence contract, so the loop restarts at the specification rather than at a new weight.

variants.title: Run the evidence loop
variants.context: The evidence loop runs from a scientific specification, through an evidence factory that versions data and solves, into a structured model, then a validation laboratory that challenges the claim, and only then bounded use with a trusted fallback.
variants.prompt: A materials group replaces its solver with a newer version whose tolerances differ. Put the work in order.

items.text: Compare the refit against analytical results and converged runs on the protected regimes.
Confirm which specified quantities, units, and tolerances the solver change actually touches.
Regenerate the affected labels and record the new solver version, mesh, and tolerance in provenance.
Restore bounded use once the envelope and the extrapolation detector match the new evidence.
Refit the learned term against the regenerated labels rather than mixing two label generations.

variants.hint: A solver upgrade can change labels without any physical change.
variants.explanation: New numerical labels are a new evidence generation, so mixing them with the old ones hides the change inside the training set.

variants.title: Build the informed model
variants.context: A physics informed model is built in four steps: specify the mathematical problem, sample observations, collocation, boundary and initial points as distinct evidence, optimize with every objective term visible, then challenge the solution against references it was not trained on.
variants.prompt: A team is fitting a physics informed model to a one dimensional heat problem. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Sample observations, interior collocation points, boundaries, and initial conditions as identifiable sets.
Optimize while tracking the data, equation, boundary, and regularization terms separately.
Define variables, units, domain, equations, known and inferred parameters, and the validation quantity.
Compare the result against analytical solutions, converged solvers, and held out parameter regimes.

variants.hint: Which step makes it possible to see one term getting worse?
variants.explanation: Evidence sets stay identifiable so each objective term can be read and challenged on its own.

variants.title: Build the informed model
variants.context: A physics informed model is built in four steps: specify the mathematical problem, sample observations, collocation, boundary and initial points as distinct evidence, optimize with every objective term visible, then challenge the solution against references it was not trained on.
variants.prompt: The same team now infers an unknown diffusion coefficient from sparse sensors. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Train while watching whether the coefficient estimate and the residual term move together or fight each other.
Check identifiability against a case with a known answer before trusting the inferred value.
Write the inverse problem: which coefficient is unknown, its units, its plausible range, and the decision it feeds.
Keep the sparse sensor observations separate from the interior residual points and the boundary set.

variants.hint: Convergence is not the same as identifiability.
variants.explanation: An inverse problem can converge to a confident wrong coefficient, so the challenge step tests a case whose answer is known.

variants.title: Build the informed model
variants.context: A physics informed model is built in four steps: specify the mathematical problem, sample observations, collocation, boundary and initial points as distinct evidence, optimize with every objective term visible, then challenge the solution against references it was not trained on.
variants.prompt: A stiff multi scale problem trains to a small loss but the fast mode looks wrong. Put the diagnostic steps in order.

items.text: Retrain with the terms tracked separately so imbalanced gradients between scales become visible.
Resample collocation points where the residual structure changes rather than only where data is dense.
Validate the fast mode against a converged reference over the full decision horizon.
Restate the domain, the scales present, and the tolerance the decision needs on the fast mode.

variants.hint: A small residual at sampled points is not a globally accurate solution.
variants.explanation: Multi scale problems hide their failure in the scalar loss, so sampling and per term tracking come before any new claim.

variants.title: Count the real cost
variants.context: Scientific utility is an end to end quantity. It includes evidence generation, training, inference, and verification cost, and it is measured at matched accuracy rather than by per call latency alone.
variants.prompt: A trusted solver takes 15 minutes per solve. Building the training set required 400 solves. The surrogate answers in 3 minutes per prediction. How many predictions are needed before the surrogate repays its data generation cost?
variants.hint: Each prediction repays only the difference between the two costs.
variants.explanation: Data generation cost 6,000 minutes and each prediction saves 12 minutes, so 500 predictions are needed to break even.

mistakes.feedback: That divides the data cost by the solver time and ignores the surrogate's own 3 minutes per call.
That divides by the surrogate cost rather than by the saving of 12 minutes per prediction.

variants.title: Count the real cost
variants.context: Scientific utility is an end to end quantity. It includes evidence generation, training, inference, and verification cost, and it is measured at matched accuracy rather than by per call latency alone.
variants.prompt: A surrogate publishes 90 percent prediction intervals. On 200 protected samples the true value falls inside the interval 162 times. What is the empirical coverage?
variants.explanation: 162 of 200 is 81 percent, which is below the nominal 90 percent, so the intervals are optimistic on this regime.

mistakes.feedback: That is the nominal level the intervals claim, not the coverage that was observed.
That is the miss rate; coverage counts the samples inside the interval.

variants.title: Count the real cost
variants.context: Scientific utility is an end to end quantity. It includes evidence generation, training, inference, and verification cost, and it is measured at matched accuracy rather than by per call latency alone.
variants.prompt: A deployment verifies one prediction in every ten against the trusted solver, which takes 20 minutes per solve. Over 300 predictions, how many minutes does the verification policy add?
variants.hint: Count the verification runs first, then price them.
variants.explanation: 30 verification solves at 20 minutes each add 600 minutes, which belongs in the speedup claim rather than outside it.

mistakes.feedback: That verifies every prediction; the policy verifies one in ten.
That is the number of verification solves, not the minutes they consume.

variants.title: Read the objective as a ledger
variants.context: A physics informed objective mixes data error, equation residual, boundary terms, and regularization with different units and scales. The weighted sum can improve while a scientifically critical term gets worse, so every component is reported in its own units.
variants.prompt: The weighted total loss fell by 30 percent, while the boundary residual reported in its own units doubled. What should the team conclude?
options: The release claim holds, because the total objective is the summary of all terms.
The boundary weight should be lowered until the total loss and the residual agree.
The release claim is not supported, because a critical term moved the wrong way.
optionFeedback: The total is a weighted mixture of different units, so it cannot arbitrate this.
Reweighting to hide the disagreement removes the only signal that reported it.
A scalar sum can improve while the scientifically critical component degrades.
variants.hint: Which number would a reviewer of the physics actually read?
variants.explanation: Every objective component is reported in its own units, because the weighted sum can improve while a required condition is violated.

variants.title: Read the objective as a ledger
variants.context: A physics informed objective mixes data error, equation residual, boundary terms, and regularization with different units and scales. The weighted sum can improve while a scientifically critical term gets worse, so every component is reported in its own units.
variants.prompt: The equation residual is near zero at every collocation point, but a converged solver disagrees with the solution between those points. What is the most likely reading?
options: The solver reference is wrong, since the residual is the direct measure of the equation.
The network needs more parameters, since capacity is what limits residual accuracy.
The collocation sampling misses the structure, so the small residual proves little.
optionFeedback: A converged solver is one of the references the claim is supposed to survive.
Capacity does not fix a sampling pattern that never looked where the error lives.
A small residual at sampled points is not evidence of a globally accurate solution.
variants.hint: Where was the residual actually measured?
variants.explanation: Residuals are only evidence where they were sampled, so collocation points are resampled where the residual structure changes.

variants.title: Read the objective as a ledger
variants.context: A physics informed objective mixes data error, equation residual, boundary terms, and regularization with different units and scales. The weighted sum can improve while a scientifically critical term gets worse, so every component is reported in its own units.
variants.prompt: Every step that lowers the data term raises the equation term, and the two have been trading places for hours. What should the team inspect?
options: The learning rate schedule, since the run has simply not converged yet.
The random seed, since the two terms are competing by chance.
Gradient conflict and the reference scales used to normalize each term.
optionFeedback: A longer run does not resolve a systematic conflict between two objectives.
Seeds do not create a persistent trade between two physical quantities.
Terms with mismatched scales fight each other, and normalization is what makes them comparable.
variants.hint: What makes two terms in different units comparable at all?
variants.explanation: Residuals are normalized with physically meaningful reference scales, and a persistent trade between terms is inspected rather than trained through.

variants.title: Separate the uncertainty source
variants.context: Uncertainty has distinct sources: measurement from instruments and observation, numerical from discretization and solver tolerance, parameter from unknown coefficients or initial states, model form from missing mechanisms, and surrogate from finite data and limited capacity.
variants.prompt: Match each uncertainty source to what produces it.

pairs.label: Measurement uncertainty
pairs.detail: Instruments, labeling, preprocessing, and observation geometry.

pairs.label: Numerical uncertainty
pairs.detail: Discretization, convergence tolerance, approximation order, and solver implementation.

pairs.label: Parameter uncertainty
pairs.detail: Unknown coefficients, initial states, or boundary values.

pairs.label: Model form uncertainty
pairs.detail: Mechanisms that the scientific model simplifies or leaves out entirely.

pairs.label: Surrogate uncertainty
pairs.detail: Finite training data, imperfect optimization, and limited model capacity.

variants.hint: Ask which intervention would reduce each one.
variants.explanation: Collapsing these into one error bar hides which intervention, more data or a better solver or a better model, would actually help.

variants.title: Separate the uncertainty source
variants.context: Uncertainty has distinct sources: measurement from instruments and observation, numerical from discretization and solver tolerance, parameter from unknown coefficients or initial states, model form from missing mechanisms, and surrogate from finite data and limited capacity.
variants.prompt: Five findings appear in one review. Match each to the uncertainty source it belongs to.

pairs.label: Measurement uncertainty
pairs.detail: A sensor was replaced and the noise floor and missingness both changed.

pairs.label: Numerical uncertainty
pairs.detail: A solver upgrade shifted the training labels with no physical change.

pairs.label: Parameter uncertainty
pairs.detail: The diffusion coefficient for this new material family has never been measured.

pairs.label: Model form uncertainty
pairs.detail: The closure term omits a mechanism that only matters above the design temperature.

pairs.label: Surrogate uncertainty
pairs.detail: Error grows in the corner of the envelope that holds the fewest training samples.

variants.hint: Two of these would not move even with unlimited training data.
variants.explanation: Naming the source points at the fix, since more samples cannot repair a missing mechanism or a loose solver tolerance.

variants.title: Separate the uncertainty source
variants.context: Uncertainty has distinct sources: measurement from instruments and observation, numerical from discretization and solver tolerance, parameter from unknown coefficients or initial states, model form from missing mechanisms, and surrogate from finite data and limited capacity.
variants.prompt: A second review reads five more findings. Match each to its uncertainty source.

pairs.label: Measurement uncertainty
pairs.detail: Two labs report different values for the same specimen under the same conditions.

pairs.label: Numerical uncertainty
pairs.detail: Halving the mesh spacing changes the reference answer beyond the stated tolerance.

pairs.label: Parameter uncertainty
pairs.detail: The initial state of the field was never observed and has to be inferred.

pairs.label: Model form uncertainty
pairs.detail: The governing equation assumes an incompressible flow that the new case violates.

pairs.label: Surrogate uncertainty
pairs.detail: Retraining with a different seed changes the prediction in the sparsest regime.

variants.hint: Ask whether the wobble comes from the world, the solver, the equation, or the fit.
variants.explanation: Each source has its own remedy, so a single error bar cannot tell a team where to spend the next experiment or solve.
